**Section D: Essay (10 marks)**

**Write an essay of about 200 and 250 words on any one of the following topics.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **Topic 1.** The problem of unemployment in any country. You may want to write about causes, effects and possible solutions.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Un essay/composition à l'examen se structure toujours en trois temps : une introduction qui présente le sujet et annonce le plan, un développement qui traite chaque idée dans un paragraphe distinct avec des exemples concrets, et une conclusion qui résume la réflexion et, si le sujet s'y prête, ouvre sur une perspective ou une recommandation ; respecter cette structure et le nombre de mots demandé (ici entre 200 et 250) compte autant, pour le correcteur, que la qualité des idées elles-mêmes.

Sujet retenu : *The problem of unemployment in any country. You may want to write about causes, effects and possible solutions.*

**Modèle de corrigé (environ 230 mots) :**

Unemployment is one of the most serious problems facing many countries today, including Cameroon. It occurs when people who are able and willing to work cannot find a job, and its consequences reach far beyond the individual who is out of work.

Several factors explain this situation. First, the rapid growth of the population produces more job-seekers every year than the economy is able to absorb. Second, many young people leave school or university with qualifications that do not match the skills employers actually need, so that jobs remain unfilled while graduates remain jobless. Third, the closure of many factories and companies, often due to economic crises, has reduced the number of available posts.

The effects of unemployment are equally serious. On a personal level, it drives many families into poverty and pushes some young people toward crime or rural exodus in search of any opportunity. On a national level, it wastes a country's human resources and increases the burden on social services.

Fortunately, solutions exist. Governments should encourage vocational and technical training so that school leavers acquire skills that match the real needs of the job market. They should also support small and medium-sized enterprises through loans and tax incentives, since these businesses create most new jobs. Finally, young people themselves should be encouraged to consider self-employment and entrepreneurship rather than waiting only for salaried positions.

In conclusion, unemployment is a complex problem with no single cause and no single cure, but a combination of better training, support for small businesses, and a spirit of entrepreneurship can considerably reduce it.

questions.enonce_markdown: **Topic 2.** Write about a feast in your family. Say what your family was celebrating and which people were invited. Describe the food and the drinks served and the reaction of some people at the end.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Modèle de corrigé (environ 220 mots) :**

Last December, my family celebrated a feast that I will always remember: the wedding anniversary of my grandparents, who had been married for forty years.

The celebration took place in our family compound in the village. Early in the morning, the women began preparing the food while the men arranged tables and chairs under a large tent borrowed from a neighbour. Many people were invited: uncles, aunts, cousins from different towns, close family friends, and even the elders of the village who had known my grandparents since their youth.

The food was abundant and varied. There was grilled chicken, jollof rice, ndolé with fish, roasted plantains, and a huge cake decorated with the number forty. As for drinks, palm wine was served to the elders as a mark of tradition, while soft drinks and fruit juice were offered to the children and young people.

Toward the end of the afternoon, my grandfather stood up and thanked everyone for coming, his voice trembling with emotion. Several guests could not hold back their tears when he spoke about the difficult years he and my grandmother had gone through together. Then the music started, and both young and old danced late into the evening.

By the time the last guests left, everyone agreed that it had been an unforgettable feast, one that reminded the whole family how important it is to celebrate love and loyalty within a family, whatever the years may bring.

questions.enonce_markdown: **Topic 3.** Imagine you are the Minister of the Environment. Write a speech that you will deliver on what people should do to protect our environment.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Modèle de corrigé (environ 210 mots) :**

Dear fellow citizens,

As Minister of the Environment, I stand before you today because our environment is in danger, and only our common action can save it.

Every day, forests are cut down without being replanted, rivers are polluted by waste from factories and households, and plastic bags litter our streets and farmlands. If this continues, future generations will inherit a country stripped of its natural resources and exposed to floods, droughts and disease.

I am therefore calling on every one of you to take concrete action. First, plant at least one tree every year; a single tree, multiplied by millions of citizens, can restore entire forests within a generation. Second, stop throwing waste into rivers and open spaces; use the dustbins and recycling points that the government is installing in every neighbourhood. Third, reduce your use of plastic bags and prefer reusable ones, since plastic takes hundreds of years to decompose.

The government, for its part, will continue to enforce stricter laws against illegal logging and industrial pollution, and will invest in clean energy projects across the country.

Protecting the environment is not the government's duty alone; it is the responsibility of every citizen, in every town and every village. Let us act today, so that tomorrow our children can still breathe clean air, drink clean water, and enjoy the beauty of our forests.

Thank you.
